title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 21 – Legal Proceedings（一般性披露政策与 materiality 门槛）
key_points: 公司声明：基于现有信息，认为任何该等法律程序、索赔、政府争议与调查的结果不会对财务状况、经营成果或现金流产生重大影响。
披露政策：若合理可能发生超过已记录金额的损失，则披露该超出金额或区间；若无法合理估计金额或区间，则说明无法估计的原因。
raw_excerpt: based upon current information, that the outcome of any such legal proceeding, claim, or government dispute and investigation will not have a material effect on our financial position, results of operations or cash flows. Where it is reasonably possible that we will incur losses in excess of recorded amounts in connection with any of the matters set forth below, we will disclose either the amount or range of reasonably possible losses in excess of such amounts or, where no such amount or range can be reasonably estimated, the reasons why no such estimate can be made.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 21 – Legal Proceedings（737 MAX 事故相关诉讼、DOJ DPA、股东派生诉讼和解、SEC 民事罚款）
key_points: 因 2018-10-29 Lion Air Flight 610 与 2019-03-10 Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302 两起事故，公司面临多项法律诉讼（multiple legal actions）。
2021 年公司与美国司法部（DOJ）签订 Deferred Prosecution Agreement，了结 DOJ 此前披露的关于 FAA 对 737 MAX 评估的调查。
2021 年与股东派生诉讼原告达成拟议和解，使公司在 2022 年第二季度收到 $219（百万美元）。
2022 年 9 月，公司了结 SEC 此前披露的与 737 MAX 事故相关的调查并同意民事罚款，产生 $200（百万美元）的 earnings charge，该款项于 2022 年 10 月支付。
对于与事故及 737 MAX 相关的剩余未决诉讼或其他事项，公司无法合理估计保险未覆盖部分的损失区间（若有）。
raw_excerpt: Multiple legal actions have been filed against us as a result of the October 29, 2018 accident of Lion Air Flight 610 and the March 10, 2019 accident of Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302. During 2021, we entered into (i) a Deferred Prosecution Agreement with the U.S. Department of Justice that resolved the Department of Justice's previously disclosed investigation into us regarding the evaluation of the 737 MAX by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as well as (ii) a proposed settlement with plaintiffs in a shareholder derivative lawsuit that resulted in the Company receiving $219 in the second quarter of 2022. In September 2022, we settled a previously disclosed investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission related to the 737 MAX accidents and consented to a civil penalty, which resulted in an earnings charge of $200 that was paid in October 2022. We cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, not covered by available insurance that we may incur as a result of any remaining pending lawsuits or other matters related to the accidents and the 737 MAX.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 21 – Legal Proceedings（Embraer 合资终止争议仲裁）
key_points: 2019 年公司与 Embraer S.A. 签订协议设立合资公司，涵盖 Embraer 商用飞机与服务业务，公司原计划以 $4,200（百万美元）收购 80% 股权，另设一家推广 C-390 Millennium 新市场的合资公司。
2020 年公司以 Embraer 未满足特定交割条件为由行使合同终止权；Embraer 对终止权提出异议，该争议目前处于仲裁程序中。
公司无法合理估计该仲裁可能产生的损失区间（若有），并预计仲裁于 2023 年末或 2024 年初完成。
raw_excerpt: During 2019, we entered into agreements with Embraer S.A. (Embraer) to establish joint ventures that included the commercial aircraft and services operations of Embraer, of which we were expected to acquire an 80 percent ownership stake for $4,200 … In 2020, we exercised our contractual right to terminate these agreements based on Embraer's failure to meet certain required closing conditions. Embraer has disputed our right to terminate the agreements, and the dispute is currently in arbitration. We cannot reasonably estimate a range of loss, if any, that may result from the arbitration, which we currently expect to be completed in late 2023 or early 2024.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 13 – Liabilities, Commitments and Contingencies（环境修复负债与合理可能超出区间）
key_points: 2022 年环境修复活动：付款净额 -$43，估计变更 +$190；2021 年：付款净额 -$59，估计变更 +$99。
已记录负债代表最佳估计或合理可能成本区间的低端，涵盖最长 30 年的运营与维护期间。
2022 与 2021 年末，合理可能修复成本区间的高端超出已记录负债的金额分别为 $1,058 与 $1,094（百万美元）。
raw_excerpt: The liabilities recorded represent our best estimate or the low end of a range of reasonably possible costs expected to be incurred to remediate sites, including operation and maintenance over periods of up to 30 years. It is reasonably possible that we may incur charges that exceed these recorded amounts because of regulatory agency orders and directives, changes in laws and/or regulations, higher than expected costs … At December 31, 2022 and 2021, the high end of the estimated range of reasonably possible remediation costs exceeded our recorded liabilities by $1,058 and $1,094.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 13 – 737 MAX Grounding 客户让步负债的构成与支付时点
key_points: 2022-12-31 的 $1.9 billion 余额中，$1.6 billion 为已签约的客户让步及其他负债，$0.3 billion 仍待与客户谈判确定。
已签约部分构成：$0.8 billion 预计通过降低客户交付付款清偿，$0.7 billion 预计以现金支付，$0.1 billion 为其他让步。

raw_excerpt: The liability balance of $1.9 billion at December 31, 2022 includes $1.6 billion of contracted customer concessions and other liabilities and $0.3 billion that remains subject to negotiation with customers. The contracted amount includes $0.8 billion expected to be liquidated by lower customer delivery payments, $0.7 billion expected to be paid in cash and $0.1 billion in other concessions. Of the cash payments to customers, we expect to pay $0.1 billion in 2023 and the remaining $0.6 billion in future years. The type of consideration to be provided for the remaining $0.3 billion will depend on the outcomes of negotiations with customers.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Note 14 – Arrangements with Off-Balance Sheet Risk（融资承诺）
key_points: 与已订购飞机（含选择权及销售活动中提议的飞机）及已交付飞机再融资相关的融资承诺合计：2022-12-31 为 $16,105，2021-12-31 为 $12,905（百万美元）。

We have concluded that no reserve for future potential losses is required for these financing commitments based upon the terms, such as collateralization and interest rates, under which funding would be provided.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K, Item 1A Risk Factors（对 Note 21 法律程序与保险覆盖的交叉引用）

See Note 21 of the Consolidated Financial Statements for discussion of legal proceedings resulting from the October 29, 2018 accident of Lion Air Flight 610 and the March 10, 2019 accident of Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302. The amount of insurance coverage we maintain may be inadequate to cover these or other claims or liabilities.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — 737 Program Highlights and Production Rate (p33, p9)
key_points: 2022 年波音将 737 项目产能提升至每月 31 架，并表示将依据市场需求与供应链能力逐步进一步提升。
737 项目在 2022 年与 2021 年分别计入 1.88 亿美元与 18.87 亿美元的异常生产成本（abnormal production costs）。
超过 190 个国家已批准恢复 737 MAX 运营；中国自 2019 年以来首个 737 MAX 客运航班发生于 2023 年 1 月 13 日。
raw_excerpt: We increased the production rate to 31 per month in 2022, and expect to implement further gradual production rate increases based on market demand and supply chain capacity. We expensed abnormal production costs of $188 million and $1,887 million during the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021. Over 190 countries have approved the resumption of 737 MAX operations.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — 737-7/737-10 FAA Certification Status (p34)
key_points: 737-7 与 737-10 型号在 2022 年末仍处于 FAA 取证（certification）过程中。
Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 修订了 ACSAA 第 116 条，使包括 737-7 与 737-10 在内的、于 2020-12-27 之前提交的原始或修订型号合格证申请不再受第 116 条机组告警（crew alerting）规格约束。
FAA 签发 737-10 型号合格证满一年后，任何新的 737 MAX 飞机须包含特定安全增强措施方可获得适航证；波音已为相关改装成本计提，且不预期该成本重大。
raw_excerpt: The 737-7 and 737-10 models are currently going through FAA certification. The Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 amended Section 116 of the ACSAA, such that applications for original or amended type certifications that were submitted to the FAA prior to December 27, 2020, including those of the 737-7 and 737-10, are no longer subject to the crew alerting specifications of Section 116. Additionally, beginning one year after the FAA issues the type certificate for the 737-10, any new 737 MAX aircraft must include certain safety enhancements to be issued an [airworthiness certificate].

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — 787 Program: FAA Delivery Authorization (p35)
key_points: 波音于 2022-07-28 获得 FAA 恢复交付授权，并于 2022 年 8 月恢复 787 交付。
787 交付曾于 2021 年 5 月至 2022 年 8 月暂停，原因是包括供应链在内的生产质量问题。
raw_excerpt: We received FAA authorization to resume delivery on July 28, 2022 and deliveries resumed in August. During 2022, we delivered 31 aircraft to customers. ... During 2021, we delivered 14 aircraft between March and May 2021 prior to deliveries being paused in May 2021 due to production quality issues including in our supply chain.

title: Boeing FY2022 10-K — Capital Resources: debt covenant compliance and substantial borrowing capacity
key_points: At December 31, 2022, Boeing was in compliance with the covenants for its debt and credit facilities.

The most restrictive covenants include a limitation on mortgage debt and sale and leaseback transactions as a percentage of consolidated net tangible assets, and a limitation on consolidated debt as a percentage of total capital.
Boeing states that, when considering debt covenants, it continues to have substantial borrowing capacity.
At December 31, 2022 Boeing had $14.6 billion of cash, $2.6 billion of short-term investments, and $12.0 billion of unused borrowing capacity on revolving credit line agreements.

In Q3 2022 Boeing entered a $5.8 billion 364-day revolving credit agreement expiring August 2023, a $3 billion three-year revolving credit agreement expiring August 2025, and amended its $3.2 billion five-year revolving credit agreement expiring October 2024.
raw_excerpt: Any future borrowings may affect our credit ratings and are subject to various debt covenants. At December 31, 2022, we were in compliance with the covenants for our debt and credit facilities. The most restrictive covenants include a limitation on mortgage debt and sale and leaseback transactions as a percentage of consolidated net tangible assets (as defined in the credit agreements) and a limitation on consolidated debt as a percentage of total capital (as defined in the credit agreements). When considering debt covenants, we continue to have substantial borrowing capacity.
